content.thinking:
Out of 1456 total tests, 1416 pass and 40 fail, matching exactly the pre-existing baseline failures — so my changes introduced zero new failures, and typecheck is clean too. Now I need to move to live behavioral verification with the isolated Postgres instance and Playwright, starting by pushing the schema to the isolated verification database.

I'll set up a minimal environment file, seed a test user directly via a small Prisma script rather than fighting the registration form's rate limits, then use Playwright to log in through the real login form, verify the session cookie and corresponding UserSession DB row, revoke the session through the Settings UI, and confirm a subsequent request with that cookie gets redirected as logged out. For team role gating, I'll create Org and Membership records directly via a script and check the UI rendering behavior for a MEMBER role against the Invite button.

Since server actions are compiled into special Next.js POST endpoints requiring the internal Next-Action protocol, directly invoking them via raw HTTP is complex — so I'll rely on Playwright clicking real UI elements as the genuine invocation path, since that's how these gated actions actually get triggered in practice.

My real proof is twofold: confirming the invite/admin UI never renders for a MEMBER role in the browser, and independently verifying via source review that `canAdministerOrg` is enforced inside the action itself, so even a hand-crafted request would fail. I considered writing a standalone script to call `updateMemberRole` directly, but these "use server" functions depend on `requireUser()` → `currentUser()` → `cookies()`, which requires an active Next.js request scope and would throw outside of one — so a plain Node script can't invoke them in isolation.

The most practical path to genuine full-stack proof is Playwright against the real dev server: log in as a MEMBER, confirm the Invite/role-editing controls don't render, then try to hit the server action's compiled POST endpoint directly (identified by the `Next-Action` header) to test defense-in-depth against a bypassed UI.

To pull this off, I'd need to capture the actual POST request sent when an ADMIN triggers the action, then replay it with the MEMBER's session cookie to see if the backend truly enforces the block rather than just hiding the button. Given the effort already invested, I'll proceed step by step: set up the environment file, push the schema to an isolated database, then build or run the dev server.

Since the full app has many external integrations like Stripe and Proxmox, a full build could hit unrelated errors, so I'll try `next dev` instead for faster, on-demand compilation of just the routes I need. I should also check next.config.ts for anything that hard-fails at boot without extra env vars, since most other files seem to load things lazily.

Given the time constraints, I'll just boot `next dev` on a scratch port and iterate on whatever errors come up. First step is setting up the .env file.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

11024	### 2026-09-21 — Game hosting-page 404 audit: raw-family-key slug bug hit 22 families, not just Space Engineers
11025	
11026	**Incident.** The owner found `https://nxeon.cloud/spaceengineers-server-hosting` returning a real 404,
11027	despite Space Engineers being a genuine hosted family (`lib/game-control.ts` GAME_CONTROL, real mod.io
11028	content imported the same night) and having a working page at the *different* slug
11029	`/space-engineers-server-hosting`. Asked to check whether this was systemic across the whole
11030	game-server marketing surface.
11031	
11032	**Root cause.** `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts`'s `GAME_URL_SLUG` map is the single source of
11033	truth mapping each `GameFamily` key to its real marketing slug (e.g. `spaceengineers` →
11034	`"space-engineers"`, `gmod` → `"garrys-mod"`, `sdtd` → `"7-days-to-die"`) — used correctly by the
11035	game×location matrix. Two NxLabs mods pages built their "see hosting plans" link from the **raw family
11036	key** instead of that map:
11037	
11038	- `app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx:402` — `` href={`/${mod.gameFamily}-server-hosting`} ``
11039	- `app/(marketing)/mods/games/[family]/page.tsx:146` — `` href={`/${family}-server-hosting`} ``
11040	
11041	Confirmed live before the fix: `curl -s https://nxeon.cloud/mods/games/spaceengineers` contained
11042	`href="/spaceengineers-server-hosting"` — the exact broken link the owner hit.
11043	
11044	**Full scope, tested against real production HTTP status for all 47 `GAME_FAMILIES`.** 22 families have
11045	a real, working `*-server-hosting` page under the `GAME_URL_SLUG`-mapped slug, but 404'd on the raw
11046	family key these two pages generated: `projectzomboid` (real: `project-zomboid`), `sdtd`
11047	(`7-days-to-die`), `vrising` (`v-rising`), `gmod` (`garrys-mod`), `conan` (`conan-exiles`), `theforest`
11048	(`the-forest`), `sonsoftheforest` (`sons-of-the-forest`), `bedrock` (`minecraft-bedrock`),
11049	`abioticfactor` (`abiotic-factor`), `corekeeper` (`core-keeper`), `arkasa`
11050	(`ark-survival-ascended`), `dst` (`dont-starve-together`), `vintagestory` (`vintage-story`), `l4d2`
11051	(`left-4-dead-2`), `spaceengineers` (`space-engineers`), `kf2` (`killing-floor-2`), `sandstorm`
11052	(`insurgency-sandstorm`), `theisle` (`the-isle`), plus the four `plutoniumt4/t5/t6/iw5` families (whose
11053	"real" slug, `plutonium-t4` etc., is ALSO a 404 — see gap below). The other 25 families' raw key already
11054	equals their marketing slug, so were never affected.
11055	
11056	**Fix applied.** Both call sites now resolve `GAME_URL_SLUG[family] ?? family` before building the href
11057	(new `hostingSlug` local in each file), matching the convention every other cross-link in the codebase
11058	already follows. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
11059	
11060	**Defense in depth — 301s for anyone who already hit the broken URL.** Added 18 permanent redirects to
11061	`next.config.ts`'s `redirects()` (naive raw-key slug → real page), following this file's existing
11062	retired-slug pattern (e.g. `/revsports` → `/`). Excludes the 4 Plutonium families and
11063	`schedule1`/`stationeers`, which have no real destination under *any* slug (see gap below — a redirect
11064	to another 404 helps no one). Verified none of the 18 redirect `source` paths collide with a real
11065	existing page folder before adding them.

2941	## Teams and organizations
2942	
2943	**What it does — stated precisely, because this used to be overstated.** An `Organization` has one
2944	owner plus a set of `Membership` rows. A membership grants **visibility of the org roster**, and for
2945	`OWNER`/`ADMIN` the right to invite, re-role and remove members. **It grants nothing else.**
2946	
2947	The docblock at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-teams.ts:17-27` is unusually blunt and worth quoting:
2948	
2949	> Servers, domains, volumes, game servers, billing and invoices all remain scoped to the account that
2950	> owns them; no loader or action anywhere joins `Membership` to a resource. The per-member "dashboard
2951	> areas" control that used to sit on this page **has been removed rather than left in place**:
2952	> `Membership.areas` was written, echoed back as saved, and read by nothing, so an owner who
2953	> restricted a member to Invoices was shown a restriction that did not exist.
2954	
2955	That removal is the right pattern for this codebase: when a control cannot be enforced, delete the
2956	control rather than leave a false affordance.
2957	
2958	**Consent is enforced.** `inviteMember` emails an invitation; only `acceptInvite`, run by the invitee,
2959	creates a `Membership` (`:29-31`). Nothing can add a person to an org they did not agree to join.
2960	Tokens are signed with a TTL (`signInviteToken` / `verifyInviteToken` / `INVITE_TTL_HOURS`, all in
2961	`/opt/nxeon/lib/team-guard.ts`). Every mutation verifies the actor holds a membership of the required
2962	role in the target org (`canAdministerOrg`), so a hand-crafted request cannot touch someone else's org.
2963	
2964	**Data model.** `Organization` (`prisma/schema.prisma:871`), `Membership` (`:880`).
2965	
2966	**Honest note.** Shared billing and cross-account resource access **do not exist**. The
2967	`emails.teamInvite` template has an `acceptUrl`, and that flow now genuinely exists — but a member
2968	still sees none of the owner's servers. No dashboard page is org-scoped.
2969	
2970	## Support tickets and live chat
2971	
2972	**What it does.** Two channels: threaded email-style tickets, and a real-time chat with attachments.
2973	
2974	```
2975	┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
2976	│  Support                                          [ + New ticket ]   │
2977	├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
2978	│  #1042  Migration left one domain dark        HIGH    ANSWERED       │
2979	│  #1039  Invoice question                      NORMAL  CLOSED        │
2980	├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
2981	│  #1042 · Migration left one domain dark                              │
2982	│  ── you · 2026-07-25 09:12 ────────────────────────────────────────  │
2983	│  studionexis.com shows a certificate warning.                        │
2984	│  ── Nxeon Support · 2026-07-25 10:40 ─────────────────────────────    │
2985	│  That domain is being served another site's certificate…             │
2986	│  [ Reply…                                              ] [ Send ]    │
2987	└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
2988	```
2989	
2990	**Entry points.** Customer `app/dashboard/support` + `app/dashboard/support/[id]`; admin
2991	`app/admin/support` + `app/admin/support/[id]`. Chat: `app/admin/chat`, `lib/actions-chat.ts`,
2992	`app/api/chat/*` (conversation, upload, attachment). Feedback widget: `app/dashboard/feedback`,
2993	`app/admin/feedback`.
2994	
2995	**Data model.** `Ticket` (`prisma/schema.prisma:170`) with `TicketStatus`
2996	(`OPEN|ANSWERED|CUSTOMER_REPLY|CLOSED`, `:73`) and `TicketPriority` (`LOW|NORMAL|HIGH|URGENT`, `:80`);
2997	`TicketMessage` (`:182`); `ChatConversation` (`:921`), `ChatMessage` (`:939`), `ChatAttachment`
2998	(`:955`); `Feedback` (`:824`). RBAC area: `support` — reachable by `SUPPORT` and `ADMIN`.
2999	
3000	### The AI chat agent (reworked 2026-08-15)
3001	
3002	The live-chat widget is a **Claude-powered agent**, not a keyword bot. Every incoming
3003	visitor message runs an agentic tool loop (`lib/kb-llm.ts` → `askClaudeWithTools`):
3004	
3005	- **Tools for everyone** (`lib/kb-tools.ts`, `PUBLIC_TOOLS`): `check_platform_status`
3006	  (live `StatusIncident`/`Announcement`), `get_plans` (authoritative catalog), `search_help`
3007	  (KbChunk full-text). **Signed-in customers** additionally get the 6 read-only account tools
3008	  (overview/services/service/invoices/billing/tickets, all scoped to `userId`) plus
3009	  `open_support_ticket` — the one write action (the safe way it escalates something it can't do).
3010	  Assemble via `chatToolsFor(userId)`; dispatch via `runChatTool(userId, name, input)`.
3011	- **Grounding:** `lib/kb-system.ts` (`KB_SYSTEM` + `KB_PAGES`) is the full-system knowledge in
3012	  the prompt. There is **no keyword-retrieval fallback** — retrieval only seeds context.
3013	- **Graceful degradation:** if the model can't run (no/invalid key, API error, over daily cap),
3014	  the bot replies with one warm human-handoff message (`degradedReply` in `lib/kb.ts`) — never a
3015	  blog snippet. Hard failures log `KbBotLog.kind = "llm_error"`; `kbActivity().llmErrors24h`
3016	  drives a red **"assistant degraded"** banner on the admin AI-settings card
3017	  (`components/admin/settings/KbAssistantCard.tsx`).
3018	- **Config:** admin Settings → AI assistant. Keys: `kb_bot_enabled`, `kb_bot_api_key` (encrypted),
3019	  `kb_bot_model` (code default `claude-sonnet-4-6`), `kb_bot_coupon`, `kb_bot_daily_cap`,
3020	  `kb_bot_max_replies`, `kb_bot_agent_email`, `kb_bot_window_sec`. **Test connection** button
3021	  (`testBotKey`) validates the key live. **Requires a valid, funded Anthropic key** — without it
3022	  the agent degrades gracefully but cannot answer.
3023	- **Widget** (`components/ChatWidget.tsx`): polls the conversation; auto-scroll follows new
3024	  messages **only when the user is already at the bottom** (so scrolling up to read history is
3025	  never yanked down).
3026	
3027	## Notifications and transactional email
3028	
3029	**Two independent channels**, and knowing which one a given event uses is the difference between "the
3030	customer was told" and "the customer would have been told if they had logged in".

```

## API tokens and the public API

**What it does.** Lets a customer mint a bearer token and call a small read-only HTTP API.

```
 customer: Settings → API keys
   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │  ci-deploy      servers:read     last used 2026-07-24  [🗑]   │
   │  monitoring     full             never used            [🗑]   │
   │  [ + Create key ]                                            │
   │  nxk_live_7f3a…  ← shown ONCE. Stored as sha256 only.        │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

 GET /api/v1/servers
   Authorization: Bearer nxk_live_… (or legacy nxe_…)
   → authenticateApiToken()   lib/api-auth.ts   sha256 lookup, stamps lastUsedAt
   → tokenHasScope(auth, "servers:read")
```

**Two credential models, both accepted — not indecision, a migration in progress (fixed 2026-09-24,
see the change history entry below).** `ApiKey` (`nxk_live_…`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, `lib/nx/account.ts`
mints it) is what Settings **actually creates today** — it is the only credential-creation UI a customer
can reach. `ApiToken` (`nxe_…`, richer array `scopes` with wildcards + `expiresAt`) is fully implemented
end-to-end in `lib/actions-tokens.ts` (create/revoke, audit-logged) and is what the admin user-detail page
displays, but its one intended customer entry point, `components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx`, is
**orphaned** — no page imports it, a leftover from before the Nexion redesign. `lib/api-auth.ts`'s
`authenticateApiToken` recognises both prefixes: an `nxk_` key is looked up in `ApiKey` and its single
`scope` string (`"full" | "servers:read" | "metrics:read"`) is translated to the array shape
(`apiKeyScopeToScopes`) the rest of the authorization logic shares with `ApiToken`.

**Entry points.** `/opt/nxeon/lib/api-auth.ts` (`authenticateApiToken`, `authenticateApiKey`,
`tokenHasScope`, `apiKeyScopeToScopes`), `/opt/nxeon/lib/nx/account.ts` (`createApiKey`/`revokeApiKey` —
the reachable customer path), `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-tokens.ts` (`createApiToken`/`revokeApiToken` —
complete but currently unreachable from any page), `/opt/nxeon/app/api/v1/servers`, UI
`components/nx/SettingsView.tsx` (live) / `components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx` (orphaned). Models
`ApiKey` and `ApiToken` (`prisma/schema.prisma`).

**Scope matching** (`lib/api-auth.ts`): the exact scope, the global `*` (what an ApiKey's `"full"` scope
maps to), the resource wildcard `servers:*`, or the generic `read` which satisfies any `*:read`.

**Fixed 2026-09-24 — empty ApiToken scopes are now read-only, not full access.** `tokenHasScope` used to
treat a token with no recorded scopes (pre-scoping legacy rows) as unlimited access; it now grants reads
only (`action === "read"`), fail-closed for anything that mutates. Survivable in practice either way
today because the public API is still one read-only route, but the empty-scopes case no longer becomes a
live problem the moment a mutating endpoint is added.

**Fixed 2026-09-24 — `GET /api/v1/servers` no longer leaks the internal NAT-bridge address.** It used to
return `Server.ipAddress`, the VM's 10.20.0.0/24 address — unreachable from outside this host and useless
(or actively misleading) to an API caller. It now returns the same connection info the dashboard itself
shows (`app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`): the node's public IP + the server's DNAT `sshPort`, or the
dedicated IP directly when the server has one; `host`/`port` are `null` for a server not provisioned yet.

   Authorization: Bearer nxk_live_… (or legacy nxe_…)
   → authenticateApiToken()   lib/api-auth.ts   sha256 lookup, stamps lastUsedAt
   → tokenHasScope(auth, "servers:read")
```

**Two credential models, both accepted — not indecision, a migration in progress (fixed 2026-09-24,
see the change history entry below).** `ApiKey` (`nxk_live_…`, `prisma/schema.prisma`, `lib/nx/account.ts`
mints it) is what Settings **actually creates today** — it is the only credential-creation UI a customer
can reach. `ApiToken` (`nxe_…`, richer array `scopes` with wildcards + `expiresAt`) is fully implemented
end-to-end in `lib/actions-tokens.ts` (create/revoke, audit-logged) and is what the admin user-detail page
displays, but its one intended customer entry point, `components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx`, is
**orphaned** — no page imports it, a leftover from before the Nexion redesign. `lib/api-auth.ts`'s
`authenticateApiToken` recognises both prefixes: an `nxk_` key is looked up in `ApiKey` and its single
`scope` string (`"full" | "servers:read" | "metrics:read"`) is translated to the array shape
(`apiKeyScopeToScopes`) the rest of the authorization logic shares with `ApiToken`.

**Entry points.** `/opt/nxeon/lib/api-auth.ts` (`authenticateApiToken`, `authenticateApiKey`,
`tokenHasScope`, `apiKeyScopeToScopes`), `/opt/nxeon/lib/nx/account.ts` (`createApiKey`/`revokeApiKey` —
the reachable customer path), `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-tokens.ts` (`createApiToken`/`revokeApiToken` —
complete but currently unreachable from any page), `/opt/nxeon/app/api/v1/servers`, UI
`components/nx/SettingsView.tsx` (live) / `components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx` (orphaned). Models
`ApiKey` and `ApiToken` (`prisma/schema.prisma`).

**Scope matching** (`lib/api-auth.ts`): the exact scope, the global `*` (what an ApiKey's `"full"` scope
maps to), the resource wildcard `servers:*`, or the generic `read` which satisfies any `*:read`.

**Fixed 2026-09-24 — empty ApiToken scopes are now read-only, not full access.** `tokenHasScope` used to
treat a token with no recorded scopes (pre-scoping legacy rows) as unlimited access; it now grants reads
only (`action === "read"`), fail-closed for anything that mutates. Survivable in practice either way
today because the public API is still one read-only route, but the empty-scopes case no longer becomes a
live problem the moment a mutating endpoint is added.

**Fixed 2026-09-24 — `GET /api/v1/servers` no longer leaks the internal NAT-bridge address.** It used to
return `Server.ipAddress`, the VM's 10.20.0.0/24 address — unreachable from outside this host and useless
(or actively misleading) to an API caller. It now returns the same connection info the dashboard itself
shows (`app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`): the node's public IP + the server's DNAT `sshPort`, or the
dedicated IP directly when the server has one; `host`/`port` are `null` for a server not provisioned yet.

input.old_string: ## Two-factor authentication — and why `lib/totp-verify.ts` is a plain module
input.new_string:
## Sessions — "Active sessions" and per-device sign-out

**What it does.** Settings lists every device signed in to the account (other than the one you're
looking at) with a real "Revoke" button per device, plus a "Sign out everywhere else" bulk action.

**Fixed 2026-09-24 — this used to be entirely decorative (0 `UserSession` rows in production).**
Nothing wrote a row when someone logged in, so the list was always empty and `revokeSession(id)`
(`lib/nx/account.ts`) — which correctly sets that row's `revokedAt` — had no row to ever act on.

- `createSession` (`lib/auth.ts`) now writes a `UserSession` row (`tokenHash` — sha256 of the session
  JWT, never the plaintext — `userAgent`, `ip` via `clientIp`, `location` via `geoLocateIp`) on every
  real sign-in: password login, register, Google/Discord OAuth, and the re-issue `changePassword` /
  `signOutOtherSessions` do after bumping `sessionVersion`. Best-effort — a geo lookup or write hiccup
  can never block a sign-in.
- `realUser()` now looks the current token up by its own hash and refuses it if that specific row is
  revoked, independent of the account-wide `sessionVersion` check. A token with **no** tracked row
  (minted before this existed, or before 2026-09-24) is treated as valid — fail-open for pre-existing
  sessions, the same precedent this file already sets for `assertSessionToken`'s `typ` claim — so
  deploying this does not mass-log-out every customer already signed in; it starts covering sessions
  from the next time each one logs in.
- `changePassword` / `signOutOtherSessions` now also revoke every tracked `UserSession` row for the
  account (besides the sessionVersion bump), so a device that sessionVersion already logged out stops
  showing as "active" too.
- Settings' session list **excludes the caller's own current session** (`currentSessionTokenHash()` in
  `lib/auth.ts`) — the list's own copy already promised this ("No other sessions", "sign out everywhere
  **else**"), and without the exclusion the very first thing real tracking would do is put an unlabeled
  "Revoke" next to the customer's own current browser that, now that revoke actually works, signs them
  out of the tab they clicked it from.

**Entry points.** `lib/auth.ts` (`createSession`, `trackSession`, `realUser`,
`currentSessionTokenHash`), `lib/nx/account.ts` (`revokeSession`), `app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx`,
`components/nx/SettingsView.tsx`. Model `UserSession` (`prisma/schema.prisma`).

**Still orphaned, not touched by this fix.** `lib/nx/account.ts`'s `revokeOtherSessions(currentTokenHash)`
— a tokenHash-scoped alternative to the sessionVersion-based `signOutOtherSessions` — has no caller
anywhere in the UI. Low priority: the live "Sign out everywhere else" button already works correctly via
the sessionVersion path, which this dead function would duplicate, not replace.

input.new_string:
**Data model.** `Organization` (`prisma/schema.prisma:871`), `Membership` (`:880`).

**Honest note.** Shared billing and cross-account resource access **do not exist**. The
`emails.teamInvite` template has an `acceptUrl`, and that flow now genuinely exists — but a member
still sees none of the owner's servers. No dashboard page is org-scoped — there is no `orgId` on any
`Server`/`Domain`/`Invoice`/etc. anywhere in the schema, confirmed by grepping the whole repo (`orgId`
appears only in `lib/actions-teams.ts`, `lib/team-guard.ts` and the GDPR export). Building real
role-gated access to shared resources would mean inventing that relationship and org-scoping every
loader and action that touches one — a real feature, not a bug fix; deliberately out of scope here,
same as when the per-member "dashboard areas" control above was removed rather than half-wired.

**Fixed 2026-09-24 — the Team UI's own copy overclaimed exactly what the paragraph above says doesn't
exist.** The "Roles & Permissions" tab's `ROLES` table said Admin manages "servers and services" and
Billing controls "invoices, payment methods and plans", under a heading reading "These are the roles the
permission system actually enforces" — directly contradicting the honest "What organisation membership
grants" note already rendered two paragraphs below it on the same panel. `BILLING` in particular has
always been functionally identical to `MEMBER` (`canAdministerOrg` only recognises `OWNER`/`ADMIN`) — the
role exists to be assigned honestly, not because it changes anything today. Copy now says so.

**Fixed 2026-09-24 — invite TTL: the token really expires at 72 hours, several places said "seven
days".** `INVITE_TTL_HOURS = 72` (`lib/team-guard.ts`) is what the encrypted invite token's own
`setExpirationTime` uses and always has been the real, enforced value (introduced whole with the
2026-09-12 stateless-invite redesign). `inviteMember`'s `OrgInvite.expiresAt` bookkeeping row —
display-only, but the "expires" date on the Invites tab reads it — was still hardcoded to 7 days, a
leftover from the ORIGINAL (pre-redesign) 7-day invite window; fixed to
`INVITE_TTL_HOURS * 60 * 60 * 1000`. `components/nx/TeamView.tsx`'s "They expire after seven days" copy
now renders the real constant via a prop (`inviteTtlHours`, sourced from `INVITE_TTL_HOURS` in
`app/dashboard/team/page.tsx`) instead of a second, driftable literal.

**Fixed 2026-09-24 — `OrgInvite.acceptedAt` is now actually set.** `acceptInvite` created the
`Membership` but never touched the invite bookkeeping row's `acceptedAt`, so it stayed `null` forever —
indistinguishable from still-pending. Since `app/dashboard/team/page.tsx`'s "pending invitations" query
already (correctly) filters on `acceptedAt: null`, an accepted invite kept showing under "Pending
invitations" alongside the person's own new membership row, for up to the invite's remaining `expiresAt`
window. `acceptInvite` now marks the row accepted right after the membership is created.

This is running unusually long, about 9 minutes in now. Since the team page hasn't been hit yet in this dev server instance, it likely needs to compile fresh, which combined with the multiple logins and wait timeouts could explain the delay.

Actually, the "Active sessions" card title should render unconditionally regardless of the sessions array contents, so the heading itself being missing is odd — I should check if the layout's "how did you hear about us" prompt might be blocking rendering of the page body entirely, and search the full page text for partial matches like "Sessions" to narrow this down.

### 2026-09-24 — Customer portal security audit: three account/security P1s (dead API keys,
decorative team roles, a session tracker that never wrote a row)

**Source.** `/root/nxeon-audit-2026-09-24/nxeon-full-audit-2026-09-24.md` §4, P1 #13/#14/#15. All
three worked on `fix/portal-security-p1-13-14-15`, branched off `main` in an isolated worktree
(`/tank/dev-worktrees/portal-security-fixes` — never built against the live `/opt/nxeon` tree). Not
pushed or deployed; committed to the branch only.

**#13 — API keys created in Settings could never authenticate.** Settings' only reachable
key-creation UI (`lib/nx/account.ts:createApiKey`) mints `nxk_live_…` in the `ApiKey` model;
`lib/api-auth.ts` only ever recognised `nxe_…` from the *different* `ApiToken` model. Every key a
customer ever generated was dead on arrival, permanently, with no error anywhere saying why.
`ApiToken` turned out to be fully implemented end-to-end (`lib/actions-tokens.ts`, richer array
`scopes` with wildcards + `expiresAt`, and what the admin user-detail page displays) but its one
intended UI, `components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx`, is itself orphaned — no page imports it,
a leftover from before the Nexion redesign. Judgment call: rather than migrate Settings onto
`ApiToken` (a UI rewrite) or leave already-issued `ApiKey` rows permanently dead, `api-auth.ts` now
accepts BOTH prefixes — `authenticateApiKey` looks up `ApiKey` by `keyHash` and translates its
single `scope` string to the array shape (`apiKeyScopeToScopes`) the existing wildcard-aware
`tokenHasScope` already understands. `ApiKey` stays the customer-facing model going forward (it's
the only one with a reachable UI); `ApiToken` keeps working for anything already minted through it.
Also fixed in the same route: `GET /api/v1/servers` returned `Server.ipAddress` — the internal
10.20.0.0/24 NAT-bridge address, unreachable from outside this host — instead of real connection
info; it now returns the same host+port the dashboard itself shows (node's public IP + `sshPort`, or
the dedicated IP), `null` for a server not yet provisioned. Also fixed while in this file: empty
`ApiToken.scopes` (pre-scoping legacy tokens) used to be treated as full access; now read-only,
fail-closed for anything that mutates.

**#14 — nothing ever wrote a `UserSession` row (0 rows in production); per-device revoke had nothing
to act on.** `lib/nx/account.ts:revokeSession` already correctly set `revokedAt` on a row — the bug
was that no row ever existed to revoke. `createSession` (`lib/auth.ts`) now writes one (`tokenHash`
sha256, `userAgent`, `ip` via `clientIp`, `location` via `geoLocateIp`) on every real sign-in,
best-effort so a geo lookup can never block a login; `realUser()` now looks the current token up by
its own hash and refuses it if that row is revoked, independent of the existing account-wide
`sessionVersion` check. A token with no tracked row (pre-existing sessions, minted before this
shipped) is treated as valid — fail-open, the same precedent this file already set for

fix/portal-security-p1-13-14-15

content.text:
All three fixes are committed, verified for real, and documented. Here's the full summary.

**Branch:** `fix/portal-security-p1-13-14-15` at commit `69ead2b11b`, in the isolated worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/portal-security-fixes` (614MB total, all on `/tank`, none of it touching the root filesystem that had the disk incident). Not pushed, not deployed.

**Bug 1 — API keys (P1 #13).** `lib/api-auth.ts` now accepts both `nxk_` (`ApiKey`, what Settings actually creates — the only reachable creation UI) and `nxe_` (`ApiToken`, fully built but its UI is orphaned dead code). `ApiKey.scope` is translated into the same wildcard-aware scope check `ApiToken` already had. `GET /api/v1/servers` no longer leaks the internal `10.20.x` NAT address — it returns the same host+port the dashboard itself shows. Also closed a related gap I found while in that file: empty `ApiToken.scopes` used to mean full access; now read-only.

**Bug 2 — team roles (P1 #15).** `canAdministerOrg` (invite/re-role/remove/cancel-invite) turned out to already be genuinely enforced — I confirmed this two ways: reading the code, and a live capture-and-replay attack (see below). The real bug was the UI copy claiming resource-level control (Admin "manages servers and services", Billing controls "invoices, payment methods and plans") that was never built and directly contradicted an honest disclaimer already on the same panel. I checked the whole schema — no `Server`/`Domain`/`Invoice` has any relationship to `Organization` anywhere — so "team-owned resources" don't exist to gate; building that is a real feature, not a bug fix, and I left it out deliberately (same call the previous author already documented making). Fixed the copy, the invite-TTL mismatch (72h real vs. "seven days" shown), and `OrgInvite.acceptedAt` never being set (which made accepted invites show as pending forever).

**Bug 3 — sessions (P1 #14).** `createSession` now writes a real `UserSession` row on every login; `realUser()` now checks per-device revocation independent of the existing `sessionVersion` mechanism, fail-open for pre-existing sessions so this doesn't mass-log-out current customers on deploy. I also caught and fixed a real consequence of the fix itself: Settings' session list now excludes the caller's own current session, or the first thing a customer would see is an unlabeled "Revoke" button that instantly logs out the tab they're using.

**Real verification, not just code reading:** typecheck clean; full suite 1418/1458 passing (same 40 pre-existing, unrelated pricing/proration failures — confirmed by stashing my changes and rerunning against the identical baseline); 34 new tests. Beyond that, I stood up an isolated Postgres instance and ran the real `next dev` server against it, driven by a real Chromium browser: two logins produced two real `UserSession` rows, clicking the real Revoke button set `revokedAt` in the database, and the revoked device's next real request was actually redirected to `/login`. For the team-role gate, I captured the real wire request a legitimate OWNER's browser sent to remove a member, then replayed that exact request with a MEMBER's session cookie, bypassing the UI entirely — the server refused it (`"You don't have permission to remove members from this organization."`), confirmed against the database.

**What's enforced now vs. still not:** per-device session revoke and both API credential prefixes are now real; team membership administration was already real and is now copy-honest; role-based access to another member's servers/billing/invoices remains intentionally unbuilt (no schema support exists for it) and the UI no longer claims otherwise.

Along the way I also found the box's root filesystem at 0 bytes free (already flagged separately, now resolved per your note) and a promotional modal (`PromoTrialPopup`) that intercepts all clicks for new-looking accounts, which I worked around in my test harness but didn't touch in the product.

result: Fixed and verified all three P1 account-security bugs (dead API keys, decorative team-role copy, and session tracking/revoke) on branch `fix/portal-security-p1-13-14-15` — real end-to-end browser+DB verification confirmed session revoke actually blocks the next request and team-role enforcement survives a raw wire-request replay bypassing the UI; typecheck clean, 1418/1458 tests passing with zero regressions; committed but not pushed or deployed.
